Your eleven projects 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He is 0.3 clear of Salah and carries meaningful upside — a quarter chance of double figures — but also real downside at 8%. The captaincy is marginal enough that it hinges on your read of this week's setup, which the model does not supply. Salah sits close enough to step in if you see reason.

You have three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That concentration is heavy but it reflects their projections, not a diversification problem in itself.

The bench projects 10.7, with Mykolenko at its head. No move cleared its points cost this week, so you are holding your free transfer. Your bank sits at £0.5m.

Your eleven projects 69.0 with the armband on Haaland, who sits 0.3 clear of Salah and carries a quarter chance of hitting double figures. The captain choice is tight but sound. Salah remains your safety net if Haaland disappoints.

You are heavy on Arsenal and Manchester City—three and two respectively in the starting eleven. That concentration works if both clubs perform, but leaves you exposed to a bad week from either. Mykolenko on the bench offers cover only to 3.1.

No transfer clears its cost this week. You have one free move and £0.5m in the bank, so any swap would need to gain more than it costs, and nothing does. Holding is the right call.

You are set to 60.8 from the bench if Haaland blanks—respectable, but hinges on your front five staying fit and on form.

Your eleven projects 69.0 with the armband on Haaland, who sits 0.3 clear of Salah and carries a quarter chance of hitting double figures. That gap is small enough that Salah remains a live option if you want to hedge; Haaland's floor is shakier, with an 8% chance of returning 2 or fewer.

You are heavily weighted to Arsenal and Manchester City, with three and two respectively. That concentration has done the work so far—Saka, Palmer and the premium forwards are your spine—but it means a blank from either will land hard. It is worth flagging, though there is no obvious fix within your transfer budget.

The bench is thin. Mykolenko at 3.1 is your only realistic cover, and even he projects well below your starters. You have one free transfer and £0.5m in the bank; nothing on the board has justified breaking even, so the recommendation is to hold and bank the transfer.

A week with good odds at the top, solid depth in midfield, and the luxury of patience.
